question: Should ClawHub sign the existing stored hosted-feed payload, and what public trust root, key id, schema version, and rollout path should OpenClaw clients trust?
rationale: Feed signing changes a client trust boundary and production secret contract, while the current spec explicitly keeps signing behind a separate key-management decision.

options.title: Sign Stored Publications
options.body: Require the signer to wrap the current `catalogFeedPublications` payload, preserve exact version/integrity semantics, and document public-key rollout before merge.

options.title: Approve A New Signed Contract
options.body: Approve a separate signed route or schema only after matching OpenClaw parser support, Vercel routing, and compatibility behavior are settled.

options.title: Pause Signing
options.body: Leave this draft parked until the server signing design, production secrets, and client trust root are ready to land together.

recommendation.title: Sign Stored Publications
recommendation.body: Require the signer to wrap the current `catalogFeedPublications` payload, preserve exact version/integrity semantics, and document public-key rollout before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the hosted feed contract and the explicit unsigned/stored-publication boundary this PR changes.
